method: read-only workflow: 6 topic auditors -> 6 adversarial verifiers -> 1 ranker; no games were run by the workflow; per-game counts are measured only where an entry says so
summary:
Ranker output for the V2-4 11e rules audit: 75 audited items from 6 topics (charges 13, movement/keywords 11, army rules 10, reserves 13, objectives 13, stratagems 15). Verdicts: 71 confirmed, 4 refuted (CH-08, ADV-02, movement CH-01, OC-11), 0 uncertain. Duplicates merged: CH-01=OW-01; CH-02=ADV-01=AR-01 (+ AR-05's RACE-1 part and the army verifier's Wazdakka RI-ASSAULT item); CH-03=HI-01; CH-05=AR-03; CH-07=AR-05 (fall-back part); CH-11=CO-03; RS-09=RI-01; CH-08's surviving part -> AR-07. The 15 ENGINE_vs_RULES items, the engine halves of CR-01/HI-02/HI-03/IB-01/CH-12/CH-09 and 4 verifier-'missed' engine defects are in engine_vs_rules (22 lines). Ranked: 51 entries, incl. 3 verifier-'missed' items whose code I re-read myself (X-FURY, X-BSFLIP, X-ENGFLAGS; not adversarially re-verified; all clear_fix=false).

13 CLEAR fixes (all AI_vs_ENGINE, high confidence, run on the 3 standard fixtures, small change behind a new FIX_ param, failing-first test given), in rank order: FIX_OBJ_AREA_REACH (OC-01), FIX_CHARGE_OW_11E (CH-01/OW-01), FIX_OBJ_AREA_ON_OBJ (OC-03), FIX_OBJ_AREA_HOLD (OC-04), FIX_EOG_TIMING (OC-02), FIX_MOVE_TERRAIN_11E (TER-01), FIX_HI_CHARGE_ODDS (CH-03/HI-01), FIX_SECURED_AWARE (OC-05), FIX_CO_NEXT_PICK (CO-01), FIX_PILEIN_TARGETS_11E (CH-09), FIX_CHARGE_REROLL_ODDS (CH-05/AR-03), FIX_ADV_ENGINE_PREDICATES (CH-02/ADV-01/AR-01), FIX_WAAAGH_ADV_REROLL (AR-06).

Bundle notes: (1) The largest family is objective hosting area vs marker (OC-01/03/04, plus RS-06 and X-BSFLIP): the AI uses centroid-to-marker 3.79in while every bench objective is a terrain area that one model controls by base overlap; build OC-01's helper first (OC-03/04 reuse it). (2) Sign-uncertain: FIX_CHARGE_OW_11E and FIX_CHARGE_REROLL_ODDS both raise charge willingness, and STATUS says the AI already over-charges ('bench T7-51 alone'); FIX_SECURED_AWARE is also sign-uncertain. V2-2 allows no switch-off arms unless the bundle crosses efficacy, so decide before the first look whether these ride in the one bundle arm. (3) V2-1 fix gate: FIX_CO_NEXT_PICK, FIX_WAAAGH_ADV_REROLL, FIX_ADV_ENGINE_PREDICATES and FIX_CHARGE_REROLL_ODDS change < ~1 decision/game; give every fix an evaluation-level tag (term/score change, as the round-5 designers did) or expect those to be parked. (4) CH-01, CH-05 and CH-04 touch the same charge-scoring functions as the round-5 charge_target finalizer: rebase together; FIX_ADV_ENGINE_PREDICATES and FIX_WAAAGH_ADV_REROLL share _should_unit_advance / RACE-1.

Bench/harness facts the parent should know (not fixed in this track): (a) Seat attribution: END_TURN_REDEPLOY (From Golden Light) for P2's unit is decided by P1's AI (AIPlayer.gd:2252 _dm(active player).decide; records log player 1 in 224/224), and evaluate_rapid_ingress never sets _current_player (profile arms read the opponent's params). Any FGL fix (RS-01) is sign-inverted in an A/B arm until the decision is routed to the owner's seat. (b) Bench rosters (AR-02) are 40kdc 1.0.19 Kult of Speed Orks and older Custodes datasheets with unattached Blade Champions, so War Horde / Lootas / [HEAVY] / 'close quarters'-tag items (HV-01, HV-02, AR-09, CQ-01) have 0 bench reach. (c) The standard Custodes bench is not reserve-free after round 1: FGL and On Gilded Wings put Allarus models into reserves (~4 placements/game in the Custodes mirror), so reserve code runs there; this changes the 'bench cannot see reserves' premise behind V2-5 parking. (d) Bench Custodes faction aggression resolves to 1.0 (FACTION_AGGRESSION_CUSTODES 1.5 never used; SEED-REAL never runs on any seat). (e) AI defenders never get the reactive shooting-stratagem window (ShootingPhase.gd:2932-2933), so defensive-stratagem fixes cannot be measured. (f) Suggested follow-up audit outside these six topics: bench Custodian Guard datasheet abilities with 11e effects the AI ignores (Praesidium Shield -1 to wound when S > T, ~22 fires/game; Stand Vigil [LETHAL HITS] on objectives, ~36/game; verifier counts), and engine-side AI policies the bench cannot A/B (Salvus 18in in CustodesKatah.gd:731-733; FURY constant score in CustodesCodexOther.gd:191-196). Reserve-fixture track candidates (0 standard reach): RS-05 (top), RS-09/RI-01, RS-08, RS-07, RS-03.

Method: read-only; I ran no games. Line numbers are for HEAD 856d61b (AIDecisionMaker.gd unchanged since e12e6e8, 27577 lines, md5 aec32113); I re-read the cited code for every clear fix and for the three added items. Per-game counts are the auditors'/verifiers' (marked 'measured' where they counted logs or records; otherwise estimates).

ranked.engine_location: MissionManager.gd:475-492 (host areas from source_pieces), 503-512 (_model_in_objective_range: any base overlap), 561-568 (model_gap_to_objective_range_px: base edge to area), 745-853 (_unit_oc_in_range per model). ranked.confidence: high (verifier reproduced every number: deployment overstatement median 3.6/4.3/4.2in; turn counts differ for 66/110, 68/170, 68/140 pairs; COORD-5 misses 48.7% of true one-move arrivals on 666 positions)
ranked.bench_fires_per_game_estimate: Every Movement plan (~10+/game, all 3 fixtures, both seats): ~550-850 unit-objective terms/game, 40-60% with a wrong turn count at deployment (measured offline on decoded saves). Changed assignments: several per game (estimate, not measured).
ranked.vp_effect: Objectives look about one turn farther away: the AI under-counts enemy units that can step onto an objective next turn (under-defends) and under-counts its own contest capacity (abandons flippable objectives as enemy_strong). Estimate +0.5 to +2 VP/game if fixed (not measured). Largest systematic mismatch found.
ranked.fix_sketch: New helper _obj_gap_px(unit, obj_pos, snapshot): when FIX_OBJ_AREA_REACH >= 0.5 and _held_dup_objective_at(snapshot, obj_pos) is non-empty, return the minimum over alive models of _held_dup_mm().model_gap_to_objective_range_px(model, entry) (0 when in range); otherwise the minimum over models of (base-edge distance to the marker - 3in), never the centroid. Use it in enemy_min_moves/friendly_min_moves, the COORD-5 reach test, e_moves/f_moves, _reachable_contest_oc and gap_in/turns_to_reach (and reuse the stored gap in _capture_arrival). Cache per (unit, objective) per plan. Param 0 returns the old centroid arithmetic exactly. Print [OBJ_AREA_REACH] with old/new values whenever turns_to_reach or projected_enemy_oc changes (evaluation-level tag for the V2-1 fix gate). Implement first: OC-03 and OC-04 reuse the helper.
ranked.test_sketch: mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy: place a 5-model Custodian Guard with its front rank 5in from area-large-2's long edge and its centroid ~12in from the marker. Param 0: turns_to_reach 2 at M6 and the unit is missing from the opponent's projected_enemy_oc. Param 1: turns_to_reach 1 and it is counted. Regression pin: with param 0 every objective-evaluation field equals today's values.

The bars were tuned on raw scores, so re-check the HI rate with the V2-1 gate.

ranked.engine_location: MissionManager.gd:141-150 (secure_objective / is_objective_secured), 917-962 (a secured lock holds with no units in range and on ties; breaks only on a greater enemy level at the end of a phase); OrkAbilities11e.gd:2384-2404 and MovementPhase.gd:5757-5768 (Gretchin THIEVIN' SCAVENGERS secures at the end of the Movement phase).
ranked.rule_ref: 14.03: 'that objective remains under their control - even once they no longer have any units within range of it - until their opponent's level of control over that objective is greater than theirs at the end of a phase'; 14.02 tie rule 'unless that objective is secured'.
ranked.bench_fires_per_game_estimate: Ork fixtures only (2 Gretchin units per Kult of Speed army): ~7 securing events per game in 2 local logs with the bench roster (reserve-variant smoke runs); est. 2-6 keeper/state decisions per Ork game; Custodes mirror 0 (no securer).
ranked.vp_effect: The Ork AI idles its best OC unit (11 Gretchin, 22 OC) on objectives the engine already holds and tries to re-take its own secured objectives; the opponent mis-counts enemy holds. Sign uncertain (a keeper also raises the bar to break the lock); estimate 0.2-1 VP per Ork game (not measured).
ranked.fix_sketch: In _evaluate_all_objectives read mm.is_objective_secured(obj_id). If secured by P and P's OC >= the opponent's: count it in P's holds and classify it for P as held_safe / held_threatened (by projected_enemy_oc); for the opponent it is enemy_weak (any greater OC flips it at the end of a phase). Skip WEIGHT_HOME_UNDEFENDED for a secured home. In the hold pass, do not require a 'sole holder' keeper on a secured objective when projected_enemy_oc == 0. Print [SECURED_AWARE]. Param 0 = ignore secured status. Own switch (sign uncertain).
ranked.test_sketch: mirror_orks_2000_postdeploy: mm.secure_objective('obj_home_1', 1, '') and move P1's models off area-large-14. Param 0: state 'uncontrolled' with the +9 home-undefended term. Param 1: held_safe, no +9, counted in my_holds; from P2's view the objective is enemy_weak.

ranked.rule_ref: 12.03 PILE-IN MOVE: 'If your unit is engaged, select every enemy unit it is engaged with ... Each model that is moved must end its move closer to the closest pile-in target'; 12.08; 03.03 coherency.
ranked.confidence: high (engine rejection messages counted in a standard bench game)
ranked.bench_fires_per_game_estimate: Measured in one standard Custodes-mirror game (seed 92001): 5 PILE_IN rejections (2 'closer to the closest pile-in target', 1 'no pile-in targets within 5in', 2 coherency) and 6 CONSOLIDATE rejections (2 '12.08 engaged with all selected', 3 coherency, others); +4 pile-in failures in an Ork-roster game. ranked.vp_effect: Pile-in and consolidation moves are lost (models stay put), so fewer models fight and fewer new engagements happen; also removes ERROR noise from the lab's no-ERROR checks. Small (not measured).
ranked.fix_sketch: With the param on, build enemy_models_info only from the engine's pile-in targets: every enemy unit the unit is engaged with, or (if unengaged) enemy units within 5in (PileInMove.before_moving, or the same test inline); return no movements when there is none (the engine accepts an empty pile-in). The per-model 'closer' test then uses the closest TARGET model, as PileInMove.model_move_allowed does. Optional second part under the same param: drop model moves that break 03.03 coherency (2 of 5 pile-in and 3 of 6 consolidation rejections in the measured game). Leave Engaging consolidation as is (the engine's all-candidates rule is itself stricter than 12.08). Print [PILEIN_TARGETS_11E] when the filter changes a destination. Param 0 = old.
ranked.test_sketch: A unit engaged with enemy A where a model of an unengaged enemy unit B is the nearest enemy model to one of its models: param 0 PILE_IN is rejected by _validate_pile_in_11e ('each moved model must end closer to the closest pile-in target (12.03)'); param 1 it is accepted and the models move toward A. mismatches.actually: At 11e nobody can fire overwatch at a charging unit. The only snap-shooting window is at the end of the charger's own Movement phase, before the Charge phase starts, so at declaration time that risk is already sunk. The penalty is a 10e carry-over with no counterpart in the engine.
mismatches.decisions_affected: Every _evaluate_best_charge call: every DECLARE_CHARGE decision, for every charger x target pair. It applies whenever the defender has >= 1 CP and any of its units with a ranged weapon is within 24", which is nearly every charge evaluation from round 2. Replica on the bench rosters while the enemy Stompa is within 24": Ork mirror Mek/Wartrike x0.08, Warbikers x0.10, Stormboyz x0.19, Deffkoptas x0.20, Wazdakka x0.30. Asym: Blade Champion x0.13, Custodian Guard x0.34, Allarus x0.37 (Ork chargers x0.43-1.0). Custodes mirror: x0.96 (Prosecutors x0.79). Estimate >= 10 affected evaluations per game in the Ork mirror and asym; the effect is small in the Custodes mirror. Not measured; the existing print tag '[OVERWATCH-RISK]' can be used for the fire census.
mismatches.vp_effect: This is the largest score distortion found. In the Ork fixtures it divides charge scores by 3-12 near a Stompa. That suppresses Custodes charges into the Ork line and Ork seeker charges, and reorders which unit charges first. Removing it means more and different charges. The VP sign is uncertain (STATUS says low-odds charges may already be over-taken), so give it its own switch inside the bundle.
mismatches.fix_sketch: FIX_CHARGE_OW_11E (0 = old behaviour): in _evaluate_best_charge, when GameConstants.edition >= 11 and the param is >= 0.5, use the neutral risk {expected_damage 0, score_penalty 1.0}. Log the old penalty with a [CH-OW-11E] tag. Failing-first test: asym save, Custodian Guard 8" from Gretchin, Ork Stompa within 24", P2 CP 2. The charge record must have no ch_overwatch_risk term, and the score must equal the score with P2 CP 0. Optional separate switch: price the real 11e exposure in movement through the existing OVERWATCH_EXPOSURE_PENALTY path (now 0); its comment at 2293-2299 is stale.

mismatches.fix_sketch: FIX_HI_ODDS (0 = old): for each candidate unit, find the engine's target per mode (leap: closest charged enemy within 12"; fray: closest enemy within 6"). Compute p = _charge_success_probability(_charge_roll_needed(d)), with p = 0 for fray when the need is above 6. Multiply the score by p, take the mode with the larger weighted score, and spend the CP only if the weighted score clears the bar. Failing-first test: one eligible Custodian Guard, nearest charged enemy 11" away, no enemy within 6", CP 3. The AI must decline. Put an enemy at 4" and it must choose into_the_fray.

mismatches.ai_assumes: A declaration pays off only if the roll reaches the declared target, as in 10e where targets were fixed before the roll. After the roll the unit must charge the best reachable unit, even when that charge is bad.
mismatches.actually: Targets are chosen after the roll from every enemy within 12" and within the roll, and the unit may decline. Value of declaring = E over 2D6 of max(0, best reachable target or combo). Example: far, high-value A and near, low-value B that cannot both be engaged. The AI misses v(B) x P(dB <= roll < dA). Its post-roll step can also commit to a charge it would never declare, for example off a held objective or into a bad trade.

mismatches.fix_sketch: FIX_CHARGE_POSTROLL (0 = old). (1) Value a unit's declaration as sum over r = 2..12 of P(r) x max(0, best value-if-reached among enemies within min(12, r), combos included), reusing the EV loop of _score_multi_target_combo with value_if = score / prob. (2) In _select_post_roll_charge_targets, return [] so that SKIP_CHARGE is sent when the best selectable value (with CH-LEAVE applied) is below the charge threshold. Failing-first tests: (a) enemies at 4" (low value) and 9" (high value) on opposite sides: the declaration score must exceed the 9"-only score; (b) a roll of 5 drops the declared target and the only selectable enemy would pull the charger off an objective it alone holds: the AI must send SKIP_CHARGE.

audit.consistent_notes:
These assumptions were checked and match the engine and 11e:
- _charge_roll_needed (AIDecisionMaker.gd:17303-17307) uses max(edge, edge - ER + terrain) - 0.02. This matches ChargeMove11e.selectable_distance_ceiling = min(12, roll), WITHIN_TOLERANCE, and ChargePhase's cost to reach the ER stop point.
- The 2D6 probability table is correct.
- Command Re-roll and free-ability re-roll answers use the 11e 'needed' distance (AIPlayer.gd:1584-1590 and 1507-1511), and charge re-rolls are in full.
- Engagement range comes from GameConstants (2\") everywhere in the charge, fight, pile-in and fall-back AI. A '1\"' appears only in comments (2224, 13886, 19973) and in the Counteroffensive proxy (CH-11).
- The T7-50 multi-target EV over 2D6 is correct for target sets that can be engaged together. The post-roll re-pick uses the engine's selectable list. The charge move generator honours 'engaged with all targets', 'no non-target in ER' and the within-1\" duty, and sends SKIP_CHARGE when no legal move exists.
- CH-LEAVE correctly assumes a failed 11e charge does not move the unit (11.02.01).
- The 11e Fire Overwatch decision (_decide_fire_overwatch_window_11e, 25418-25450) acts in the movement_phase_end window. It models snap 6s, and [TORRENT] auto-hits as RulesEngine resolves it. The 10e charge-time and per-move overwatch handlers are unreachable at 11e.
- Heroic Intervention eligibility comes from the engine list. The AI's mode-to-target logic (_hi_target_for_unit_11e) mirrors _closest_hi_target_11e, and the Into the Fray cap of 6 is known.
- Counteroffensive cost is read from the live definition (2 CP).
- Crushing Impact uses the 11e maths: T dice, 5+ for a mortal wound, capped at 6, self mortal wounds on 1s.
- The retaliation term correctly gives the charger Fights First (11.04).
- The consolidation mode order and gates (Ongoing/Engaging within 3\", terrain-aware Objective within 3\") match ConsolidationMove.select_mode.
- Fall-back destinations end outside 2\" ER, and the Desperate Escape note for battle-shocked units follows 09.07.
- The disembark charge bonus applies only when the transport did not move, matching 18.04 (Tactical vs Rapid Disembark).
- RACE-1's own-unit charge reach (M + 12\") and the 12\" close-melee threat ring are correct.

Known gaps with no bench impact:
- The movement overwatch-exposure knob is off (OVERWATCH_EXPOSURE_PENALTY 0), and its comment at 2293-2299 is stale.
- The CCW fallback in _estimate_melee_damage contradicts 11e 04.01 (models without melee weapons cannot make melee attacks), but every bench unit has a melee profile.

verdicts.reaches_bench: Every Heroic Intervention: 2-7 per game measured (see CH-03). Engine track only.

missed: [ENGINE_vs_RULES, with an AI_vs_ENGINE effect] Heroic Intervention VEHICLE rule. The validator at ChargePhase.gd:3775-3788 rejects any VEHICLE without WALKER: 'VEHICLE units cannot use Heroic Intervention unless they have the WALKER keyword' (10e rule; the 10e text is also at StratagemManager.gd:528). 11e 15.11 allows CHARACTER/WALKER vehicles, and the engine's own 11e window list does too (StratagemManager.gd:4361, 5106). The AI picks from that list (AIDecisionMaker.gd:26295) and its +2 CHARACTER bonus (26342) ranks Wazdakka Gutsmek (VEHICLE CHARACTER) first, at score 9.1. The USE action then fails with an ERROR, and AIPlayer.gd:2640-2647 declines the whole HI instead of trying the next unit. Measured: 4 rejections in one local game with the Ork bench roster (debug_20261031_035535.log, 04:01:19-04:02:20). This reaches the Ork mirror and the asym Ork seat.

[AI_vs_ENGINE] The AI reads flags in the Charge phase that the engine does not set then. FightPhase writes flags.is_engaged only on entry and clears it on exit (FightPhase.gd:317, 3883-3900, 265, 3905-3915). No code writes flags.has_charged (the engine uses charged_this_turn). Effects: (1) the FOCUS-CHARGE gang-up bonus at AIDecisionMaker.gd:18012 never fires during the Charge phase. (2) SEED-REAL at 18048 and 18050 would count engaged units, which 11.02 makes ineligible to declare a charge, and failed chargers (dead on the bench, see the faction item). (3) _build_phase_plan at 3809 reads unit.state.is_engaged, which does not exist, so engaged units get charge intents.

[AI_vs_ENGINE] _compute_pile_in_movements has no coherency check, although its docstring (AIDecisionMaker.gd:20085-20092) claims one. The code at 20200-20330 has none, and the engine requires 03.03 coherency (2" to a mate AND 9" to every model). In one standard Custodes-mirror bench game, 2 of 5 PILE_IN rejections and 3 of 6 CONSOLIDATE rejections were coherency failures. Each is retried with no movement (AIPlayer.gd:2511) and logs an ERROR line, which also adds noise to the lab's 'no ERROR' checks.

[AI_vs_ENGINE, surviving part of CH-08] The threat zones leave out the enemy advance-and-charge reach. AIDecisionMaker.gd:27171 uses M + 12 + ER, with no D6 Advance for Kult of Speed SPEED FREEKS (OrkDetachments11e.gd:616-617; ChargeMove11e.gd:51-57) or for riled-up Orks (FactionAbilityManager.gd:461). Their real reach is M + D6 + 12, so the zones are on average 3.5" short (6" at worst) in the Ork mirror and on the Custodes seat in asym.

[Not a rules mismatch, but it sets charge behaviour] Bench Custodes faction aggression resolves to 1.0. _get_player_faction_name (AIDecisionMaker.gd:2546) finds no Custodes name: the saves have no game_config army, units have no faction_keyword, and the keyword check covers only ORKS and WORLD EATERS. So FACTION_AGGRESSION_CUSTODES = 1.5 (2464) is never used. Local logs have 108 '[FACTION] Charge threshold reduced by faction aggression 1.2' lines and none at 1.5, although Custodes units evaluated charges. Effects: no charge-threshold reduction for Custodes (17558-17561), Custodes get the 2.0/5.0 gang-up values, and SEED-REAL (gated at >= 1.5 at 18028) never runs on any bench seat (0 [CHARGE-COORD-SEED] lines).

[AI_vs_ENGINE data model, low] The model field 'wounds' is the maximum and 'current_wounds' is the current value, but AIDecisionMaker.gd:26144 (Counteroffensive) and 25709 (_score_defensive_stratagem_target) read 'wounds' as the current value. So their 'badly wounded' and 'nearly dead' terms never fire.

audit.topic: ADVANCE, [ASSAULT], [HEAVY] and movement-relevant weapon keywords (Advance roll and its after-effects, Assault/Heavy/Rapid Fire/Pistol-Close-Quarters/Torrent/Blast, moving through terrain, one Normal move per phase, Fall Back). Audited file: 40k/scripts/AIDecisionMaker.gd at TIP (md5 decd649b, branch claude/awesome-clarke-31p54m), checked against the engine and .ai_lab_work/rules11e/core_rules_11e.txt. Evidence comes from 34 partial bench-fixture debug logs already on disk (charge_r5/replay_debug_logs, charge_r5/game_lens, ~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/40k/logs) and from offline geometry replays I ran (/tmp/audit_adv/*.py). No games were run and the repo was not changed.

mismatches.rule_ref: 09.06 Advance move, AFTER MOVING: 'Until the end of the turn, unless otherwise stated, your unit is not eligible to declare a charge or start an action.' 10.04 Normal shooting, ELIGIBLE IF: '...did not make an advance move this turn.' 10.05 Assault shooting: 'You can only select [ASSAULT] weapons to make attacks with.' 11.02: 'It made an advance or fall-back move this turn.' Orks Waaagh! (fixture text) grants the exceptions only 'While a unit is riled up'.
mismatches.ai_assumes: A unit whose ability texts contain 'advance' and 'charge' can always charge after an Advance. A unit whose texts contain 'advance' and 'shoot' can always shoot every weapon after an Advance. In Orks_2000 the advance-and-charge match is true for all 20 units, from the Waaagh! army-rule text. The advance-and-shoot match is true for Lootas A/B/C, Burna Boyz A/B and Tankbustas: Waaagh! supplies 'advance', and 'Shooting phase' in Dat's Our Loot!, Pyromaniaks and Rokkit Barrage supplies 'shoot'. Result: these units Advance on objective trips 'with no shooting penalty' and skip the charge-reach guard, even with targets in weapon range.
mismatches.actually: Outside a War Cry (riled-up) turn, the engine lets an advanced Ork unit fire only [ASSAULT] weapons and declare no charge. Lootas, Burna Boyz, Tankbustas, Kommandos, Gretchin, Meks and Battlewagons have no [ASSAULT] weapon, so they cannot shoot at all. Log debug_20261031_000357.log (charge_r5/replay_debug_logs): L3390 War Cry ends; L3853 'Lootas Gamma [movement]: chose Advance obj_home_1'; L3885, L4539 and L5118 Lootas, Burna Boyz and Lootas advance; in the next Shooting phase (L5641-6202) they report _can_unit_shoot(... advanced=true), and P2's only shooters are Battlewagon Beta, Beast Snagga Boyz and Tankbustas. V12's FIX_WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE intentionally keeps the text test at these two sites (wt_v12 AIDecisionMaker.gd:1707-1723).
mismatches.decisions_affected: Fires in every Ork seat (both seats of the Orks mirror, P2 of Custodes vs Orks) and 0 times in the Custodes mirror: Blade Champions are attached in every bench log and make 0 movement decisions of their own. In the 34 available partial bench-fixture logs (about 42 Ork movement phases) I counted 66 Advances by Ork units without any [ASSAULT] ranged weapon, none inside a logged War Cry window. 40 of them were by Lootas, Burna Boyz and Tankbustas; for these the text test pre-empts the targets-in-range check, and only the round-1 no-man's-land or uncontrolled-priority branches would also have advanced them. That is about 1 per Ork movement phase, or several per Ork seat per game. Treat this as an estimate: the logs are weighted to mid-game turns.
mismatches.vp_effect: Negative for Ork seats. Each case gives up the whole shooting activation of a 10-model Lootas, Burna or Tankbusta unit (or a charge) for about 3.5" of extra movement. Unmeasured, but it is probably the largest rules mismatch in this topic for the Ork fixtures.
mismatches.fix_sketch: FIX_ADV_ENGINE_FLAGS (0 = text test). In _should_unit_advance and _should_unit_advance_long_trip, replace the unit_has_ability_containing pairs with EffectPrimitivesData.has_effect_advance_and_charge(unit) and has_effect_advance_and_shoot(unit), plus V12's _rile_pending_on_selection for Keep Huntin'!-style riles. Count a unit whose ranged weapons are all [ASSAULT] (_ri_ranged_all_assault) as losing no shooting. Failing-first tests: (1) Lootas with Waaagh! text, no flags, enemy 30" away, long trip: _should_unit_advance_long_trip must return false (today true). (2) Boyz unit, gap M+1", enemy in weapon range, no flags: _should_unit_advance must return false (today true). (3) Same as (2) but with flags.effect_advance_and_charge: still true.

mismatches.ai_location: AIDecisionMaker.gd:13822-13865 _path_blocked_by_terrain: every terrain polygon (any category, area or feature, any height) is impassable unless can_move_through lists a unit keyword (only INFANTRY) or the unit has FLY. Used by _find_unblocked_move_enhanced 13335-13398. mismatches.engine_location: MovementPhase.gd:7285-7313 _get_movement_terrain_penalty: TerrainManager.calculate_movement_terrain_penalty (581-614, a flat 2" per difficult_ground piece) plus _get_vertical_climb_cost (7321-7351, ascent only, at the destination). MovementPhase.gd:7092-7112 with TerrainManager.gd:1216-1234 and 1292-1297: only solid DENSE FEATURES taller than 2" block a non-INFANTRY move; areas never block. TerrainManager.gd:500-578, the charge cost the AI uses instead, adds 1x or 2x the piece height for every piece taller than 2".
mismatches.rule_ref: 13.06 Terrain and Movement: 'Exposed/Light: All models can move horizontally and vertically through exposed and light terrain features.' Non-INFANTRY models are stopped only by dense terrain features with sections over 2" in height.
mismatches.ai_assumes: A VEHICLE or MOUNTED unit cannot cross or enter any terrain piece, including light features and terrain areas (which in 11e are also the terrain objectives). Leaving or crossing a piece costs 1x or 2x its height ('tall' = 6") as if climbing, so for example 8" to drive out of a tall area.
mismatches.actually: The engine charges that Battlewagon 2" (difficult ground; descent is free) and does not block area or light pieces. Example: log debug_20261031_014651.log L7715 (and the same position in 015117 and 002136): 'AI_MOVE_DEBUG Battlewagon Beta: centroid=(1216,333) target=(970,970) move_px=400.0 ... final_vec_len=80.0'. My offline replay of the AI's geometry on purge_the_foe_vs_priority_assets_1 reproduces 80.0px exactly. The direct path crosses the dense wall corner-ruin-right-29 (both AI and engine block it). The AI's 30° detour only exits area-large-25 (dense AREA, 'tall'), but the AI prices it at 8" (6" climb plus 2") and moves 2.0". The engine would price the same path at 2" and allow 8".
mismatches.decisions_affected: Orks fixtures only: Battlewagon x2 (VEHICLE), Warbikers x2 and Deffkilla Wartrike (MOUNTED). Every Custodes unit is INFANTRY. In the logs, 10 of 82 unique vehicle and bike move plans ended below half of M, and 3 sit exactly on the 2.0" floor. The other cut moves (for example 12" to 4", or a Wartrike cut to 3.5") match the same penalty arithmetic. The blocking rule also stops these units from planning moves into terrain-area objectives.
mismatches.vp_effect: Ork vehicles and bikes lose up to 6" or more on affected moves, which slows Battlewagon delivery and bike objective grabs. Small to moderate, negative for Ork seats; unmeasured.
mismatches.fix_sketch: FIX_MOVE_TERRAIN_11E (0 = current). In _compute_movement_toward_target and the per-model cap, price Normal and Advance moves with the engine's movement cost: calculate_movement_terrain_penalty with the unit's keywords, plus an ascent-only climb at the destination (same logic as MovementPhase._get_vertical_climb_cost). In _path_blocked_by_terrain and _find_unblocked_move_enhanced, block only what TerrainManager.can_move_through_11e blocks. Failing-first test: a Battlewagon at (1216,333) on purge_the_foe_vs_priority_assets_1, heading to (970,970), must plan at least 7.5" (today 2.0"), and the engine must accept the staged move.

audit.consistent_notes:
These assumptions match the engine and the 11e rules:

- **Enemy charge threat:** M + 12\" + 2\" engagement range, with no Advance (AIDecisionMaker.gd:26775-26800). Keeper-release reach adds +6\" for an Advance only when flags.effect_advance_and_charge is set (9343-9345). Both match 11.02.
- **RACE-1 long-trip Advance (12086-12129):** prices lost shooting and charge reach correctly. With FIX_RI_ASSAULT=1 it treats all-[ASSAULT] units as losing no shooting. Only the text-test lines are wrong (ADV-01).
- **Advance roll:** _long_trip_advance_saves_turn uses exact D6 probabilities. Planned advance destinations at M+2\" are re-planned for the real cap after the roll (AIPlayer.gd:1637-1675), so the '+2.0 average' comment is a planning heuristic, not a rule error.
- **Advance re-rolls:** the free Waaagh! re-roll is taken on 1-3; the Command Re-roll on a 1 (or a 2 with spare CP). Both are sensible.
- **Keyword maths:** [TORRENT] auto-hits; [BLAST] adds +1 attack per 5 models (no [BLAST X] in the fixtures); [RAPID FIRE X] and [MELTA X] apply at half range (closest-model approximation of the engine's per-model check); [HEAVY] is ignored for [TORRENT] weapons.
- **[BLAST] targeting:** never at engaged targets, matching 04.02 and 17.03.
- **[PISTOL]/[CLOSE-QUARTERS] either/or:** applied per model in _sanitize_shoot_assignments (206-225), matching 24.07.
- **Fall-back:** only when engaged; a battle-shocked unit must take Desperate Escape (hazard roll fails on 1-2, per 06.03). Fall-back destinations use the 2\" engagement range. The AI assumes a fallen-back unit cannot shoot or charge unless an effect allows it.
- **Transports:** a transport that advanced cannot be disembarked from (8277-8279), matching 18.04.
- **One Normal move per phase:** enforced by MovementPhase._normal_moves_this_phase (618-627); the AI never plans a second one.
- **Charge terrain cost:** the AI uses the same TerrainManager function as ChargePhase, so AI and engine agree for charges (the engine-vs-rules gap is TER-02).

Not listed as mismatches:

- **Leader-pairing text detection** (AIAbilityAnalyzer.gd:258-272) reads Swift Onslaught as advance-and-charge, adding +0.15 at AIDecisionMaker.gd:4286-4287. The bonus is the same for every bodyguard a champion could join, so it cannot change which bodyguard is chosen; I found no effect on decisions.
- **Fall-back-and-X text detection** uses the 10e wording 'fall back'. No fixture ability contains 'fall back' or 'fall-back', so the bench never reaches it.

AI_vs_ENGINE (FLY): AIDecisionMaker.gd:14211-14212 treats any FLY unit as passing all terrain, and AIDecisionMaker.gd never sends payload.take_to_skies. The engine blocks FLY non-INFANTRY models on dense features taller than 2" unless they took to the skies (MovementPhase.gd:1139-1146 and 7092-7112; TerrainManager.gd:1216-1234). On the bench this means Deffkoptas, FLY VEHICLE, x2 per Ork side. Also, the per-model cap (AIDecisionMaker.gd:14423-14424) charges FLY units a diagonal climb (TerrainManager.gd:528-536), while the engine charges FLY movement 0 (MovementPhase.gd:7292-7293). No Deffkoptas 13.06 rejections observed, so reach is low.

ENGINE_vs_RULES (report only): FLY units move through enemy models on Normal and Advance moves (MovementPhase.gd:747-753) and pay no terrain cost (7292-7293) without declaring take to the skies. 11e 21.03 gives these benefits only to a unit that takes to the skies, with 2" subtracted from its maximum distance. Bench: Stormboyz x4 and Deffkoptas x2 per Ork side.

AI_vs_ENGINE (opposite direction to TER-01): a model can end inside a tall difficult-ground area after the AI's collision and formation adjustments. The engine then charges difficult ground plus the ascent (MovementPhase.gd:7285-7351), which the AI's plan did not price, so staging fails and a partial move is confirmed. Example: Warbikers A m3, 'Distance 17.4" exceeds cap 12.0"', '1/3 models failed staging for U_WARBIKERS_A, confirming partial move' (asym_2000_reserves_postdeploy smoke s2). About 1-3 such engine cap failures with a terrain penalty per Ork game.

mismatches.ai_assumes: If a unit's ability texts contain 'advance' and 'charge', the unit can always charge after an Advance. If they contain 'advance' and 'shoot', it can always shoot after an Advance. Every Ork unit matches: the Waaagh! text says 'advance'/'charge' in both the 10e text on the bench saves and the 11e codex text. Blade Champions match: the bench text is 'Martial Inspiration: ... gains the Advance & Charge ability', and the codex 'Swift Onslaught' says 'Re-roll advance rolls. Re-roll charge rolls.' Bench Stormboyz also match through 'Full Throttle: ... Advance & Charge'. Advance-and-shoot is wrongly true for Orks_2000 Lootas x3, Burna Boyz x2 and Tankbustas (Waaagh! gives 'advance', another ability gives 'Shooting phase'). mismatches.actually: The engine lets a unit charge after an Advance only while it is riled up (War Cry flag), when it is a Kult of Speed SPEED FREEKS unit, or under another explicit grant. Martial Inspiration does nothing in 11e. Swift Onslaught is only a re-roll. After an Advance a unit can shoot only [ASSAULT] weapons, unless a rule grants [ASSAULT]. So the AI's 'no downside' Advance throws away the charge (non-riled Stormboyz, Gretchin, Mek, Blade Champions) and/or the whole shooting phase (bench Stompa; sweep Lootas and Tankbustas).
mismatches.decisions_affected: Bench (decoded saves). Orks fixture: all 17 units per side pass the text test, but the engine allows advance-and-charge only for the 9 SPEED FREEKS. So the false positives per side are Stormboyz x4, Gretchin x2, Mek and Stompa; the Orks mirror has them on both sides and asy has them on P2. Custodes fixtures: 3 standalone Blade Champions per side. AI-GAP-4 changes only when an objective gap falls in (M, M+2] for a unit with ranged weapons (Stompa, Gretchin, Stormboyz). RACE-1 changes on multi-turn trips with an enemy within M+12" (Stormboyz, Gretchin, Mek, Blade Champions). My estimate is 1-3 decisions per affected army per game; I did not measure it. It can be counted from the print at AIDecisionMaker.gd:11876, 'has Advance and Charge — advancing allows charge', by adding it to AI_LAB_KEEP_LOG_GREP. The chase-gate part is already in the lab records: [WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE] fired 31 times in 21 Custodes-mirror games (STATUS 02:26). Sweeps (Orks_2000) also contain the Lootas/Burna Boyz/Tankbustas advance-and-shoot false positives; there are many 'Lootas ... advances toward' a_did lines in results_r4 and results_r5.
mismatches.vp_effect: A fix removes Advances that cost a charge or a full shooting phase. The chase-gate part alone was measured by the lab at s7468 Stormboyz Normal move +6.14 [3.08, 9.19] over 36 seeds (I did not run this). The AI-GAP-4 and RACE-1 sites are unmeasured. I expect a small gain, under 0.5 VP pooled. It is not guaranteed: some racing Advances may be worth more than the lost charge. mismatches.rule_ref: Orks RULES.md:76: 'War Cry (Once per battle, per army): At the start of the Command phase, you can use this ability. If you do, friendly ORKS units with the Waaagh! ability are riled up until the end of the next turn.' The text does not say 'your'. Riled up gives 5+ InSv, ranged [ASSAULT], and an advance that does not prevent a charge.
mismatches.ai_assumes: The 10e Waaagh!: it can be called only at the start of YOUR Command phase and lasts until your next one, and its value is melee damage. So the AI calls it in round 2 at the latest and never in the opponent's Command phase.
mismatches.actually: The 11e War Cry can be used at the start of either player's Command phase and covers that turn and the next. It has no melee bonus: its value is a 5+ invuln for one enemy turn plus [ASSAULT] and advance-and-charge for one Ork turn. If called at the start of the enemy's Command phase, it protects the army in the enemy turn BEFORE the Ork turn and still covers the Ork turn. The AI never considers this.
mismatches.decisions_affected: One timing decision per Ork army per game (Orks mirror x2, asy P2). One War Cry window is also declined in every enemy Command phase until the Waaagh! is used, about 2-4 per game.
mismatches.vp_effect: Sign unknown, small: one decision per game. It moves the 5+ invuln from the enemy turn after the Ork charge turn to the enemy turn before it. It helps most when Ork units already start the enemy turn inside enemy shooting or charge range.
mismatches.fix_sketch: FIX_WAR_CRY_TIMING (0 = always pass). Put it in AIDecisionMaker.decide_window_stratagem, before ork11e_det.ai_decide, by intercepting the RULE_WAR_CRY offer; the bench swaps only AIDecisionMaker.gd. Use the War Cry when the AI would call it at its next own Command phase anyway (its round >= 2, or round 1 with units in reach) and at least N Waaagh! units are within enemy weapon range or charge reach now. Test: enemy Command phase, round 2, 4 Ork units within 18" of enemies: use=true at param 1, pass at 0.

audit.consistent_notes:
CONSISTENT. (1) The 10e Waaagh! +1S/+1A is gated off in 11e in every AI estimate: AIDecisionMaker.gd:2854-2859, 17955-17988, 19024-19031, 19534-19536, through FactionAbilityManager.gd:537-543. Only the comment at 6284-6286 still lists it. (2) The riled-up 5++ is read through EffectPrimitivesData.get_effect_invuln in _get_target_invulnerable_save (AIDecisionMaker.gd:23194-23222). (3) While a War Cry is active, effect_advance_and_charge and [ASSAULT] are real flags (FactionAbilityManager.gd:462-468), and the AI's flag checks read them correctly. The War Cry is once per battle and expires 'at the end of the next turn' (OrkArmyRules11e.gd:185-224); the AI assumes no duration. (4) The ka'tah policy in CustodesKatah.gd:695-744 uses the engine's own 11e windows (KATAHS at :94-140). It spends one ka'tah per readied step and follows the Dacatarai/Rendax split for MONSTER/VEHICLE targets. (5) On Gilded Wings (CustodesDetachments.gd:1100-1175) follows the rule: end of the opponent's Fight phase, unengaged TERMINATOR unit. A lift in the final turn is harmless. (6) Unleash the Lions (AIDecisionMaker.gd:6363-6395) asks the engine whether it can be used on that unit and fits the rule. Engine nit: CommandPhase.gd:686-688 offers it by unit NAME (ALLARUS/AQUILON), not by the TERMINATOR keyword. (7) The 10e-named heuristics in _score_faction_stratagem_use ('ERE WE GO, MOB RULE, GRAB AND BASH '+1S/+1A', VIGILANCE ETERNAL) cannot be reached for 11e codex stratagems, because _codex_for_strat (24156-24170) handles them first. (8) KEEPER-RELEASE (9320-9348) ignores an unused Waaagh! and Kult of Speed reach, but FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE is 0.0 (:1610), so it is inactive. (9) The Space Wolves doctrine pick obeys once per battle.
COSMETIC (engine, player-facing text only): CommandPhase.gd:1512 and FactionAbilityManager.gd:138-144 still say '+1 S/A melee' for the 11e Waaagh!.
CAVEATS. I ran no games, as the task forbids. All per-game counts are estimates from the decoded fixtures and the code paths; the only measured numbers are the lab's own from STATUS.md and the V12 comment. Every fix must go in AIDecisionMaker.gd, because the bench swaps only that file; changes in AIAbilityAnalyzer.gd or codex files apply to both seats and cannot be measured.
For the reach gate, these log substrings can be counted: 'has Advance and Charge — advancing allows charge', 'has Advance and Shoot', 'advancing to arrive a turn sooner', '[WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE]', 'Ability reroll (Swift Onslaught)', 'free Waaagh! advance re-roll', 'KAPTARIS —', 'DACATARAI —', '[WAAAGH] Calling'.
Most important for protocol v2: the ship-gate fixtures are not the custodes_lions and Orks_2000 named in the task (see AR-02).

verdicts.evidence: Line numbers below are from the current shipped file (1.56.8, e12e6e8, V12 C_waaagh); the audit's numbers are from an older revision. AI: AIDecisionMaker.gd:12241-12254 builds adv_and_shoot and adv_and_charge from the flag OR a text test, then returns true early (prints at :12249 and :12253); :12256-12257 'not has_ranged -> true'; RACE-1 text tests at :12464-12476; chase-gate text test at :2739-2741, gated by FIX_WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE=1.0 (:1726). The comment at :1709-1725 says AI-GAP-4 and RACE-1 keep the text test on purpose. AIAbilityAnalyzer.gd:79-91 matches a substring in the ability name or description. Engine: EffectPrimitives.gd:836-859. FactionAbilityManager.gd:458-466 sets effect_advance_and_charge and effect_advance_and_shoot only while riled up, and :489-498 clears them. OrkDetachments11e.gd:616-617 gives advance-and-charge to Kult of Speed SPEED FREEKS only. ChargePhase.gd:2011-2050: an advanced unit can charge only with has_effect_advance_and_charge. The 11e 'Full Throttle' (OrkAbilities11e.gd:1752-1770) needs turbo/shokk/pulse abilities, which bench Stormboyz do not have, so it does nothing. tests/test_custodes_abilities_11e.gd:1268-1270 confirms there is no Martial Inspiration row. Rules: core 09.06 'Until the end of the turn, unless otherwise stated, your unit is not eligible to declare a charge or start an action'; 10.05 'You can only select [ASSAULT] weapons'; Orks RULES.md:76 allows advance-and-charge only while riled up. I decoded the 3 fixtures: all 17 Ork units per side match the text test (10e Waaagh! text 'gains the Advance & Charge ability') and 9 of them are SPEED FREEKS. 3 Blade Champions per Custodes army match through Martial Inspiration. Only Warbikers match advance-and-shoot, legitimately (printed assault, Speed Freeks). Orks_2000 (sweeps): Lootas, Burna Boyz and Tankbustas match advance-and-shoot, confirmed by script.
verdicts.reaches_bench: The code runs on the bench, but it rarely changes a final decision there. Measured in one local V10 game (Custodes mirror, seed 92001, log godot2026-10-31T04.04.14.log; I ran no games): the AI-GAP-4 advance-and-charge early return printed 4x, all for Blade Champions. They have no ranged weapons, so :12256-12257 returns the same 'advance' anyway. For melee-focused units (Stormboyz, Gretchin, Mek and Blade Champion by _is_melee_focused_unit :2573), the pass-2.5 chase gate (:10950-11000) replaces the objective action with ATTACK whenever an enemy is inside the chase cap (20" or M+14). That covers both AI-GAP-4's 'enemy in weapon range' case and RACE-1's 'enemy within M+12' case. Pass-3 support only ever issues move or hold. Decisions that can still change on the bench: (1) the Stompa (not melee-focused) with an objective gap in (10,12]: it Advances and loses all its shooting; its RACE-1 answer is unchanged because of its 100" range; (2) horde Gretchin in R1-2 with the nearest enemy 12-18" away (FACTION_AGGRESSION_ORKS 1.2 < 1.5 makes the chase gate return {} at :2717-2724). My estimate, not measured: far below 1 decision-changing event per game pooled. A V2-1 fix gate would need a tag at evaluation level.
verdicts.corrected_description: The mismatch is real. Corrections: (1) The chase-gate site is already fixed in the SHIPPED AI (1.56.8, FIX_WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE=1.0). Only the AI-GAP-4 site (:12241-12254) and the RACE-1 site (:12464-12476) remain. (2) For units with no ranged weapons (Blade Champion, Mek), the AI-GAP-4 text test changes nothing. (3) The bench has no advance-and-shoot false positives. (4) '1-3 decisions per army per game' is too high for the bench. Pass 2.5 overrides the affected objective actions of every melee-focused unit. The visible bench cases are the Stompa (AI-GAP-4) and horde Gretchin in R1-2 (RACE-1). For Gretchin the sign is unclear: their charge is rarely worth more than the race. The War Horde Lootas, Burna Boyz and Tankbustas case affects the sweeps only.

verdicts.corrected_description: Confirmed, but this is a bench-fixture DATA mismatch, not an engine defect. The engine is right for its inputs, so report it as bench data (report only). The audit also misses part of the picture: the bench is a hybrid. A 10e row whose name matches an 11e slug gets the 11e effect by name: Blade Champion 'Swift Onslaught' (charge and advance re-roll; see AR-03 and AR-06); every Ork 'Waaagh!' (11e free advance re-roll and War Cry); 'Martial Ka'tah' (11e readied ka'tahs; see AR-04); Custodian Guard 'Stand Vigil' (11e [LETHAL HITS] against non-MONSTER/VEHICLE units in objective range, CustodesAbilities.gd:473-476); and 'Praesidium Shield' on a non-CHARACTER (11e -1 to wound when S > T, CustodesAbilities.gd:557-570). The 11e text, wahapedia Datasheets_abilities.csv:105: 'This unit can: Re-roll advance rolls. Re-roll charge rolls.' The bench Blade Champion has 'Swift Onslaught' by name. verdicts.reaches_bench: Custodes mirror (both sides) and asy (P1); 0 in the Orks mirror. Measured in one local V10 Custodes-mirror game (seed 92001): 39 'Charge eval Blade Champion' lines (20 distinct). 24 of them were at plain p 8-28% (needs of 9-11", where the re-roll adds the most). There were 6 Swift Onslaught re-roll offers and 2 re-rolls taken. That is at least 1 affected evaluation per game pooled. Decision flips: not measured.
verdicts.corrected_description: Confirmed. One detail for the fix: AIPlayer.gd:1508-1512 re-rolls only when the roll misses the NEAREST target. So 1-(1-p)^2 is exact only for the nearest target. For a farther target the true value is p_far*(2-p_near), which is lower. Direction: the lab's charge evidence says the AI already over-charges, so a fix that makes Blade Champions charge more has an uncertain sign.

verdicts.reaches_bench: Orks mirror (both sides) and asy P2, the 9 SPEED FREEKS units. Fall-back part: changes only when an engaged SPEED FREEKS unit stands on an objective; off an objective it falls back anyway (:11714 onwards). RACE-1 part: Deffkoptas x2 walk when an enemy is within 24"; Wartrikes x2 walk when an enemy is within 12"; Wazdakka walks through the raw-flag RI-ASSAULT re-check (:12493-12498) when an enemy is within 26". The engine lets all of them Advance, shoot with [Assault] and charge. Mostly R1-2 long trips. Not measured; plausibly about 1 per Ork army per game.
verdicts.corrected_description: Confirmed, with corrections. (1) fb_and_charge changes only the ON-objective branches. Switching it on makes a SPEED FREEKS unit that is winning OC, or is the only holder, fall back (:11655-11690). The fall-back executor tries the full M (12") first (fractions 1.0..0.25), moving directly away from the enemy when the target is the objective it stands on (:11786-11870). A charge back would then need about 10-12" (17% or less), so this half is likely HARMFUL, not 'sign unknown'. (2) Per 09.07 and 10.05, [Assault] after a fall-back does not allow shooting. The engine correctly leaves Kult of Speed out of has_effect_fall_back_and_shoot (EffectPrimitives.gd:814-823). Only fb_and_charge is wrong. (3) The RACE-1 part also covers Wazdakka through the RI-ASSAULT re-check at :12493, which reads the raw flag (see missed).

Not measured; probably under 1 flip per Ork army per game.
verdicts.corrected_description: Confirmed. Minor point: the 2" AI-GAP-4 band is not an 'average'. It equals the plain-D6 P(>=2) = 0.83 margin. With the re-roll the same reliability is P(>=3) = 0.83, so (M, M+3] is the consistent widening. Blade Champions get the same re-rolled distribution.

Threat data is built every movement phase (:6901), the phase plan every turn, and the gang-up seed in charge scoring. verdicts.corrected_description: Confirmed, with corrections. (1) Own planned reach is M+12 plus an ER allowance (:3834), not plain M+12. (2) The +ER term is a 10e carry-over. In 11e the target must be within the roll itself, so for ordinary enemies the AI zone is 2" too generous (which partly offsets centroid measurement), and for advance-chargers it is short by D6-2 (up to 4"). (3) The gang-up filter also wrongly skips SPEED FREEKS units that FELL BACK. (4) The Salvus 18" rule is short against ANY enemy with M > 6, not only advance-chargers: Stormboyz and Speed Freeks reach 24-26" and the Stompa 22" without advancing. It is engine-side policy that the bench does not swap, so report only.

audit.consistent_notes: Consistent (AI = engine = 11e): per-model ingress stand-off reads GameConstants 8in (AIDecisionMaker.gd:8159-8172 vs IngressMove.gd:53,73-92); denial radius value 8in from GameConstants (26532-26562, F007); Deep Strike may land in the enemy DZ and is exempt from the round<3 DZ ban (7955-7990 vs IngressMove.gd:103); arrivals only when the engine offers PLACE_REINFORCEMENT (round>=2, MovementPhase.gd:4179) and RI only when offered at the end of the opponent's Movement phase from round 2; P2-80 DS-first for SR units with Deep Strike matches engine placement_type (MovementPhase.gd:4191-4196); 50% points cap incl. attached leaders and FORTIFICATION exclusion match FormationsPhase/20.01; arrived units may charge the same turn (neither AI nor ChargePhase blocks, 20.04); main-path arrivals enforce 11e coherency (2in + 9in envelope); Arae-Shrike 12in ring and SM-11e Omni-scrambler retirement mirrored; plan arrival_round validated 2-3 (PlanValidator.gd:56-57); round-3 destruction with repositioned exemption implemented (ScoringPhase.gd:972). Not mismatches (capability gaps): AI never uses Infiltrators set-up, Scouts-from-reserves (SCOUT_RESERVES_DEPLOY), Aerial Manoover/Da Jump (scored 0). KEEPER-RELEASE reserve threat (9329-9395) ignores edge band/DZ ban but FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE = 0. Engine does not implement 20.01.02 end-of-battle destruction; no VP effect (no destroyed triggers). Method: read-only, I ran no games. Bench reach from 224 cus-mirror 11e records (bench_data/ai_versions_11e_2026-10-29, fixture sha b5f75f85 = tracked fixture; FGL/RI/arrival code unchanged since) and current-code probe logs in /tmp/resv_research (written by the reserve-fixtures workflow); 8-vs-9in and denial-gap numbers from Python replicas (/tmp/audit_res/scripts/prefilter_sim.py, denial_sim.py) on rollout-case saves. Key context: postdeploy fixtures start with 0 reserves, but Custodes repositioning (FGL, On Gilded Wings) puts ~3 units/game into reserves in the cus mirror; the Orks mirror shows no reserve activity; asym numbers are estimates.

verdicts.reaches_bench: Custodes mirror: 1.0 per game (224/224, P2 seat, round 1 only). Asym: 0, because the Custodes are P1; the offer comes at the end of P2's turn and P1's next turn is in the next round. Orks: 0 (no FGL). Pooled 0.33 per game, below the V2-1 gate of 1.0.
verdicts.corrected_description: Correct as stated. Two additions. (1) The AI docstring at AIDecisionMaker.gd:21115-21117 says the offer comes 'at the end of the owner's turn'. The engine offers it at the end of the opponent's turn, which is why the second player gets an offer in round 1. If FIX_FGL_NEXT_TURN is benched with M1/M2 profile arms, it switches the opponent's unit and the sign of E is inverted.

missed: HARNESS (high priority, affects benching of every reserve fix). Reserve decisions for the non-active player run under the ACTIVE player's AI. The END_TURN_REDEPLOY for P2's unit at the end of P1's turn is decided by AIPlayer.gd:2252 _dm(player).decide(...) with player = the active player; the acting-player logic at 2005-2085 has no case for this offer. AIDecisionMaker.gd:21200 only passes the owner as an argument. The records confirm this: the R1 FGL is logged with player 1 in 224/224 Custodes-mirror games. evaluate_rapid_ingress (AIDecisionMaker.gd:26578, called at AIPlayer.gd:1263) never sets _current_player; only decide() sets it (2953). So every get_param inside it (in _score_reserves_deployment, FIX_HELD_DUP at 7938, REINFORCE_* at 8120-8136) reads the profile of the active opponent (1459-1464) when both seats share the AIDecisionMaker class, which is the case in profile arms. run_paired.py:16-19 uses M1 = P1 base / P2 candidate, M2 swapped, E = (M1-M2)/2. With that design, a FIX_ in these paths (RS-01 FIX_FGL_NEXT_TURN, an RS-02 Rapid Ingress guard, RS-03/05/06 changes on the Rapid Ingress path) switches the OPPONENT's unit, and the bench reports the effect with inverted sign. This reaches every Custodes-mirror game (P2's R1 FGL and P2's R2 Rapid Ingress).

AI_vs_ENGINE (the engine is also wrong against 20.04). AIDecisionMaker.gd:21143-21151 allows the FGL 'escape' in any round and 'reposition' while battle_round <= 3. But when a first-player unit uses FGL at the end of the second player's round-3 turn, ScoringPhase.gd:584-587 and 966-974 destroy it: only flags.repositioned_to_reserves is exempt, and FGL sets strategic_reserves_redeploy (1336-1340). The unit survives only by an ordering quirk when it is the LAST pending offer: _handle_end_turn_redeploy calls _handle_end_turn at 1378 before its own diffs are applied. Bench (224 Custodes-mirror records): 14 such FGLs; 9 were followed by further offers, and 7 of those 9 units never acted again (about 0.03 per game). The same can happen in asym, where the Custodes are P1.

ENGINE (the AI follows it). Units destroyed at the end of round 3 keep status IN_RESERVES: ScoringPhase.gd:993-1000 only sets models.alive=false. GameState.gd:523-529 get_reserves_for_player has no alive test, so MovementPhase.gd:7743-7781 still offers PLACE_REINFORCEMENT for the dead unit. _validate_place_reinforcement (MovementPhase.gd:4140-4259) has no alive-model check, and all-null positions skip every per-model test. AI _decide_reserves_arrival (7646-7848) has no alive check either, and _check_formation_coherency returns true for 0 positions (23405-23406). So the AI spends a Movement decision 'arriving' a dead unit. Bench: the round-4 'Allarus Custodians arrives from Deep Strike' records that follow the destructions in the previous item. VP effect about 0, but it pollutes the decision records used by the critics.

AI_vs_ENGINE (not stated in RS-05). The Rapid Ingress CP is spent at USE (MovementPhase.gd:2484), before the placement is validated, and AIPlayer.gd:1344-1349 has no retry or alternate for a failed PLACE_RAPID_INGRESS_REINFORCEMENT. So the missing coherency and wall checks in the AI's Rapid Ingress loop (AIDecisionMaker.gd:26702-26729) cost 1 CP and leave the unit in reserves. Bench: 0 observed.

Minor premise. The _evaluate_end_turn_redeploy docstring (AIDecisionMaker.gd:21115-21117) says FGL is 'offered at the end of the owner's turn', but the engine offers it at the end of the opponent's turn (ScoringPhase.gd:1253). The 'escape' rule (21145: wounds 50% or less and enemies within 12in, described as 'in next-turn charge reach') is therefore mistimed: the owner acts next and can move away before any enemy charge. Escape was used 41 times in 224 Custodes-mirror records (0.18 per game).

Record accuracy (not a rules mismatch). _decide_reserves_arrival and evaluate_rapid_ingress store centroid = positions[0] (AIDecisionMaker.gd:7801 and 26752) even when an alternate candidate pi was the one placed. The decision record's spot_in and nearest_objective_in (7835-7843) and the Rapid Ingress log then describe the wrong spot, which misleads critic review of reserve arrivals.

audit.topic: Objective control (OC) and timing: hosting area vs marker, range, level of control, secured objectives, battle-shock OC, when primary/secondary VP score. When measuring distances to and from an objective, measure to and from the closest part of it.' 14.02: 'A model is within range of a terrain objective while it is within that terrain area.' 01.04: 'measure to or from the closest part of that model's base.' 01.04.01: 'A unit is within a specified distance if one or more of its models are within that distance.'
mismatches.ai_assumes: A unit reaches or contests an objective when its centroid comes within 3.79in (3in plus the 20mm marker radius) of the objective's marker point. Every gap, moves-to-range, one-move-threat and contest-capacity estimate is centroid distance minus 151.5 px (comment 9702: 'a unit takes an objective when a model is within control range of the marker').
mismatches.actually: On the bench, and on every official 11e layout in the critic corpus, each objective is a terrain area. The engine counts a model as soon as any part of its base overlaps that area, and one model is enough. Along the deployment axis the area extends 5.75in (large areas) or 5in (centre) from the marker. Measured at deployment, the AI overstates the gap by a median of 3.6in (custodes), 4.3in (orks) and 4.2in (asym), p90 5.2-6.0in. The area accounts for a median 2.2-2.4in of that and centroid-vs-nearest-base-edge for 1.8-2.1in. turns_to_reach differs for 66/110, 68/170 and 68/140 unit-objective pairs. 'Reachable this turn' (gap at most M) flips for 4, 22 and 10 pairs. On 666 mid-game positions (tests/rollout_cases, same official layouts), the COORD-5 one-move test misses 7367 unit-objective pairs that are within M+2in of the area: 49% of the true one-move arrivals, mean 11 per position, with only 5 false positives. RACE-1 moves-to-range differ for 41% of pairs (25925/62982). RI-RACE (_ri_enemy_next_move_oc 12356-12399) already measures nearest model to hosting area, so the AI applies two different reach rules to the same objective.
mismatches.decisions_affected: Every Movement-phase plan uses it. It drives the objective state: enemy_weak (+7) vs enemy_strong (-5) depends on contest_oc. It also drives the COORD-5 OC need, keeper sufficiency, the RACE-1/RACE-SKIP/LONE-TRIP race tests, the per-extra-turn distance penalty, the round-1 'unreachable' -2, the Advance-on-long-trip choice, and capture-pass ordering. Volume: about 10 plans per game x 11-17 units x 5 objectives, i.e. 550-850 unit-objective terms per game, 40-60% of them with a wrong turn count. Several assignments per game probably change (estimate; not measured). A fix log tag would easily pass the V2-1 gate of 1 or more lines per game.
mismatches.vp_effect: Objectives look about one turn farther away than they are. The AI under-counts enemy units that can step onto an objective next turn, so it under-defends held objectives. It also under-counts its own contest capacity, so flippable objectives are marked enemy_strong and abandoned. Estimate: +0.5 to +2 VP per game if fixed (not measured).
mismatches.fix_sketch: FIX_OBJ_AREA_REACH (0 = current arithmetic). Add helper _obj_gap_px(unit, obj_pos, snapshot): when _held_dup_objective_at() returns an entry, the minimum over alive models of MissionManager.model_gap_to_objective_range_px(model, entry); otherwise the minimum over models of (base-edge distance to marker - 3in). Use it in enemy_min_moves/friendly_min_moves, the COORD-5 reach test, e_moves/f_moves, _reachable_contest_oc and the candidate gap_in, and store gap_in so _capture_arrival reuses it. Cache per (unit, objective) per evaluation. Log [OBJ_AREA_REACH] when turns_to_reach or projected_enemy_oc changes. Failing-first test on mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy: place a 5-model Custodian Guard with its front rank 5in from area-large-2's long edge and its centroid about 12in from the marker. Today turns_to_reach is 2 at M6 and the unit is missing from the opponent's projected_enemy_oc. With the fix it is 1 and counted.

audit.consistent_notes:
These AI assumptions match the engine and the 11e rules (AIDecisionMaker.gd@e12e6e8 unless noted):
1. Level of control is a per-model OC sum via MissionManager.model_oc. AI: _unit_oc_at_position 12546-12571 and _ai_model_oc 12536. Engine: MissionManager.gd 651-688 and 745-853.
2. Battle-shocked units add 0 OC now, group-aware for attached units (AI 12549-12555 = MM 699-700, 763-777). Undeployed and reserve units add 0 (AI 12556-12558).
3. Control needs a strictly higher level and a tie is uncontrolled (AI 8963-8981 = MM 903-913). The exception is secured objectives (OC-05).
4. With FIX_HELD_DUP=1, these already use MissionManager's hosting-area predicate: the current-OC pre-pass (8813-8822), already_on_obj (9714-9717), COORD-2 incoming (9638-9641), the projection skips for units already in range (8910, 8946), LONE-FLIP (10376, 10980) and RI-RACE (12356-12399).
5. Objective consolidation (12.08) uses MissionManager.model_within_inches_of_objective (20446-20573).
6. Command-rule timing: awareness includes Command rules one round early (21452-21454). The engine scores Command conditions at the end of the Command phase in rounds 2-4 and at end of turn in round 5 (MM 1138-1141, 1822-1823). Contest capacity uses one move in round 5 (8957-8958).
7. The central objective is the 'central' designation at the exact board centre in all 3 fixtures and all 666 critic positions; AI is_central (within 4in of centre, 9098) agrees. Home and enemy home by zone (8984-8985) match MM 2867-2876.
8. Table quarters (01.04.05): _get_table_quarter and _get_covered_quarters (22820+) use 'wholly within one quarter and more than 6in from centre', which mirrors SecondaryMissionManager._check_table_quarter_presence.
9. 11e battle-shock persistence and recovery are implemented in the engine (CommandPhase.gd 344-349, 401-423, 1139-1146) and documented in the AI (24612-24620). Only the projections ignore them (OC-06).
10. Engine 'within a terrain area' means base overlap (MM 503-512), which matches 01.04.01. The open-ground range of 3in plus 20mm, measured from the base edge (MM 787-840), matches 14.01.01; the AI constant of 151.5 px equals it, but the AI measures from model centre or centroid (OC-01, OC-04).
11. The engine's secured-lock break (a greater enemy level at the end of a phase, with mid-phase refreshes keeping locks; MM 917-940) matches 14.03. Thievin' Scavengers secures after an end-of-movement control check (MovementPhase.gd 5757-5768).
12. The 15 VP per turn and 45 VP total primary caps exist in both the AI and the engine; only the cap's scope differs (OC-09).
13. F009 battle-shock denial (BATTLE_SHOCK_DENIAL_WEIGHT=0), FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE (0) and VIGILANCE ETERNAL (Shield Host, not a bench detachment) also contain marker-distance tests but are inactive on the bench.
14. All bench fixtures: every objective is terrain-hosted (source_pieces), and the bench rotates the 25 disposition pairings by seed (--rules11e).

Arithmetic: per_obj_vp = 3+3 = 6, window 6 x holds capped at 15, so marginals are 6, 6, 3, 0; the engine pays 3 per non-enemy-home objective.
verdicts.reaches_bench: Rare. Determined Acquisition games: 4/42 cus, 4/42 asy, 2/40 ork look-1 seeds. hold_new exclude_home (Purge and Secure, Unstoppable Force): 9/42, 9/42, 6/40, and only while that side's home is unheld. The V2-1 gate seeds (91001/91101/91201) give P1 Unstoppable Force but never Determined Acquisition.

verdicts.evidence: CommandPhase.gd 149-157: check_all_objectives at phase entry, before the battle-shock tests. 1110-1160: _resolve_battle_shock_test writes flags only. 2564-2619: 2596 apply_sticky_objectives and 2606 score_primary_objectives run on the entry-time state (comment 2602). MissionManager.gd 1129-1142 does no re-check, and 128-130 re-determines control only after phase_completed. Rules 14.02.01 (core_rules_11e.txt 1179) and 08.05 (754-755).
verdicts.reaches_bench: Engine-only; no AI decision. It changes VP whenever a unit in range changes battle-shock status in its own Battle-shock step: about 1-3 per Ork game, fewer in the Custodes mirror.

verdicts.evidence: AIDecisionMaker.gd 21522-21537: per_obj_vp collects per_objective rules of any 'when'. 21588-21605: marginal against the window. 21624-21645: the window counts only when=='command' (21633). Engine MissionManager.gd 1716-1722 (window reset at Command entry) and 3270-3299 (the 15 cap covers command, eot and eot_any). Outmanoeuvre (PrimaryMissionData11e.gd ~392-402) in R4-5: EOT hold_enemy_home 10 + per_objective 6 (exclude_home only excludes own home) gives 16, clipped to 15, so a second non-home objective adds 0. The AI prices it at 6 because its window is 0: the command per_objective rule is R2-3 only.
verdicts.reaches_bench: Rare. Outmanoeuvre appears in 2/42 cus, 2/42 asy, 1/40 ork seeds; other near-cap EOT cases are infrequent. It never appears in the V2-1 gate seeds.
verdicts.corrected_description: Precise form of the defect: EOT per_objective VP is priced against the 15 cap, but against a window that counts only command per_objective/hold_min VP. Same-turn EOT awards and all hold_enemy_home/hold_central/hold_min/hold_new VP never fill the window.

verdicts.evidence: AIDecisionMaker.gd 22749-22756 (Forward Position hints 'enemy_home' 5 + 'nml' 2.5), 22768-22772 (Centre Ground hint 'central' 4), 21612-21616 ('nml' = not home and not enemy home, so it includes obj_center). Engine SecondaryMissionManager.gd 1654-1666 (Forward Position pays for the enemy home or designation 'expansion') and 1116-1154 (Centre Ground = model within 3in of the centre point with no enemy within 3in/6in); SecondaryMissionData.gd 514-532 and 561-580. Bench obj_center has designation 'central'; nml_1/2 are 'expansion'. The bench uses the 18-card 11e tactical deck (SecondaryMissionData.gd 669-678; AIBenchmarkRunner.gd 346-354) with 2 draws per turn and no hand limit.
verdicts.reaches_bench: Yes, whenever Forward Position or Centre Ground is in hand (random draw; Forward Position shuffles back in round 1). Each such plan adds +3 (Forward Position) or +4.8 (Centre Ground) to obj_center. In 2 of 3 local Ork games, the VP-stakes lines list FP/CG among obj_center's top sources 9 and 2 times. The effect on decisions is unmeasured.
verdicts.corrected_description: Frequency is likely understated. 'Under 1 decision per game' is not supported: both cards are in the 18-card bench deck, and local logs show the hint active in several plans in some games. The rest is accurate.

verdicts.evidence: AIDecisionMaker.gd 9007-9013: round 1 gets +3 on every objective (+1 for uncontrolled NML), with the comment 'scoring starts in round 2', which means rush now because round-1 positions are scored next. 9076-9083: round-1 retention bonus 'don't abandon early captures before scoring starts'. The card-driven estimator already handles the timing: 21449-21454 prices command rules from the preceding round via scores_next, and EOT rules in their own round. Engine MissionManager.gd 1129-1141 and 1815-1827. Only the round-2 comments at 9014 and 9020-9022 ('FIRST scoring round', '+1.2 ... for first VP scoring') misstate the mover's timeline: its own round-2 Command scoring happens before its round-2 Movement.
verdicts.reaches_bench: The weights run in every round-1/2 plan in all fixtures, but there is no rule-level estimate that the engine contradicts.
verdicts.corrected_description: The AI does not assume round-1 positions do not score. The remaining issue is a mislabelled heuristic in round 2 (9014-9025). That is a tuning question for the parameter-tuning track, not a clear rules fix.

verdicts.evidence: MissionManager.gd 414-446 (write at 443); 382-386 (_secured_lock_break_enabled = phase_end); 917-924 (mid-phase returns the OC leader and keeps locks). check_all_objectives(false) is called at MovementPhase.gd 3706/3724/3745/3762/4763 and ChargePhase.gd 1485. Rules 14.02.01 (1179) and 14.02 (1163). The AI reads objective_control_state only at 22010-22030 (_assess_tempting_target, Command/Scoring phases).
verdicts.reaches_bench: The engine state changes mid-phase in every game, but no bench AI decision reads it mid-phase.

verdicts.evidence: AIDecisionMaker.gd 9843-9851 and 9347-9352: scoring_chances = MAX - arrival_round, which is 0 for a round-5 arrival, then floored at 0.05 (1915). Gated by get_param('MOVE_REACH_HORIZON', 0.0) (1914); FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE is 0.0 (1611); ai_config.json sets only PLANS_ENABLED. Engine MissionManager.gd 1137-1140 (R5 command scoring deferred) and 1822-1823 (scored at R5 EOT).
verdicts.reaches_bench: No. Both gates are 0 by default and no bench profile sets them. The defect is latent.

missed: AI_vs_ENGINE, reaches the Ork fixtures: _battle_shock_flip_value (AIDecisionMaker.gd 24666-24684) decides whether a target holds an objective by model CENTRE within 3.79in of the marker (24674). It sums friendly, enemy and target OC with _get_oc_at_position/_unit_oc_at_position without the board entry and mm (24680-24684), so area holders are missed (same defect as OC-04). Also, 24702 passes "is_central": not is_home and not is_enemy_home, so both expansion objectives are priced as central (hold_central rules and 'central' hints pay on them). The engine pays hold_central only for the designated central objective (MissionManager.gd 2675 -> _get_central_objective_id_11e 2878-2883). Bench reach: SQUIG FLINGIN' (Kult of Speed, StratagemManager.gd 227) is scored via AIDecisionMaker.gd 25006-25043 -> _best_battle_shock_target 24736-24750 in every Ork Movement phase.

AI_vs_ENGINE, reaches Custodes mirror and asym P1: _evaluate_end_turn_redeploy (AIDecisionMaker.gd 21123-21131 and 21150) is the From Golden Light decision for Allarus Custodians. Its 'holding an objective' guard is centroid within 3.79in of the marker, and 'stranded' is centroid-to-marker > 15in. An Allarus unit on an objective area with its centroid more than 3.79in away is not protected by the guard and can be re-dropped off an objective it controls (escape branch at 21145: wounds <= 50% and an enemy within 12in). The engine offers the redeploy at the end of the opponent's turn (ScoringPhase.gd 1245-1300). It is once per battle, so low frequency.

AI_vs_ENGINE (OC-03 family), all fixtures: _evaluate_insane_bravery (AIDecisionMaker.gd 24773-24781) adds +3 value only when the unit centroid is within 3.79in of a marker. Units holding by area are under-valued. The auditor mentioned this only inside OC-08.

AI_vs_ENGINE: the A Tempting Target hint (AIDecisionMaker.gd 22685-22689) adds 'nml' 2 VP to every NML objective, including the centre. The engine pays 5 VP only for the single opponent-selected tempting_target_id (SecondaryMissionManager.gd 1242-1248; SecondaryMissionData.gd 234-238; when_drawn opponent_selects_objective). The AI already reads that id, but only for discard decisions (22010-22030). Active whenever the card is in hand (18-card 11e deck).

AI_vs_ENGINE, low impact: the Secure No Man's Land hint (AIDecisionMaker.gd 22678-22683) prices 2.5 VP per NML objective, linearly. The 11e engine pays a flat 5 VP only for 2+ NML objectives, with no 1-objective tier (SecondaryMissionData.gd 210-215). So the first NML objective is worth 0, the second 5 and a third 0.

AI_vs_ENGINE, low frequency: the hold_min/per_objective exclude_home pricing assumes home is held whenever anything is held (AIDecisionMaker.gd 21547-21549 counted = my_holds-1; 21629-21630 non_home = my_holds-1). The engine counts the actual non-home controlled objectives (MissionManager.gd 2847-2865). When the mover holds a non-home objective but not its home (21 of 410 movement positions in the 666-case corpus), an extra non-home objective is priced as 'reaches hold-1' (4 VP) although hold-1 is already met. 18 cards carry command hold_min min 1 exclude_home.

ENGINE_vs_RULES (report only): Burden of Trust tests 'within range' as base edge within 3in + 20mm of the marker point, not the hosting terrain area (SecondaryMissionManager.gd 1430-1448 _count_guarded_objectives, 2232-2261 _auto_assign_guards, 2343-2358 prompt), against 14.01/14.02 (core_rules_11e.txt 1153, 1162). On bench terrain objectives a guard standing on the area more than 3.79in from the marker does not score and is not auto-picked.

AI_vs_ENGINE, little or no bench reach: other OC-at-marker callers without the area predicate are _assess_burden_of_trust (AIDecisionMaker.gd 22222-22223, secondary discard) and _find_best_scout_objective (5957-5958; no bench unit has Scouts). Also decide() 3004-3010 sets profile rule_context.on_objective by centroid; it matters only if a profile rule conditions on on_objective.

mismatches.engine_location: ChargePhase.gd:607-611 (edition>=11: logs '[11e 15.08] no Fire Overwatch against charging ...' and makes no offer); StratagemManager.gd:174 (CORE_WINDOW_STRATAGEMS: fire_overwatch_11e only in movement_phase_end), 5079-5093 (timing opponent/movement/end_of_phase), 4197-4216 (fire_overwatch_shooter_reason_11e rejects TITANIC and engaged shooters); MovementPhase.gd:1699-1702 (no per-move offer at 11e)

The charge score is multiplied by 0.2-1.0 (x0.8 more for a CHARACTER, x0.5 more if overwatch could kill half the unit).
mismatches.actually: At 11e no Fire Overwatch exists in the Charge phase. The engine skips it and logs that. Fire Overwatch is only used at the end of the charger's own Movement phase (before the charge), and never by TITANIC or engaged units. The penalty prices a risk that cannot happen. This is the T7-51 term found in earlier rounds; it is still not gated at e12e6e8. New detail: the shooter that causes most of the penalty in the Orks fixtures is the TITANIC Stompa, which cannot use Fire Overwatch under any timing.
mismatches.decisions_affected: Every charge-target evaluation, in all 3 fixtures. Orks mirror smoke game (seed 92001, 7736b71): 92 [OVERWATCH-RISK] lines, 86 of them 'extreme' from the Stompa (penalties x0.30/x0.19/x0.08). Example: 'Charge eval Stormboyz Beta -> Wazdakka Gutsmek: prob=58%, target_score=4.5, ow_risk=4.4(extreme), final=0.3', then 'No charge worth declaring (best score: 0.3, threshold: 0.4)'. That game had 17 such rejections, and only 3 DECLARE_CHARGE against 115 SKIP_CHARGE. Custodes mirror: 96-183 evaluations per game, mostly x0.96-0.99, some x0.49-0.86. Asym: the Custodes chargers are penalized for the Ork Stompa.
mismatches.vp_effect: Orks fixtures: Ork charges are strongly suppressed (score x0.08-0.30). Removing the penalty gives more Ork charges. Probably the largest VP effect in this topic for the Orks mirror and asym (estimate, not measured). Custodes mirror: small.
mismatches.fix_sketch: FIX_NO_CHARGE_OVERWATCH (0 = old). When >=1 and GameConstants.edition >= 11, skip _estimate_overwatch_risk at 17375 (penalty 1.0), so the ch_overwatch_risk multiplier at 17462 is never applied.
